esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the thoracic cage and pectoral region during horizontal adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with the back supported. Begin with both elbows flexed and the fists positioned beside the chest. Extend both arms forward at chest height, pause briefly, then flex the elbows to return.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Seated Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Thoracic Expansion
esercizi.description: This breathing exercise is intended to improve controlled respiratory mechanics of the thoracic cage and pectoral region, with emphasis on horizontal abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand. Extend your arms forward in front of you, with your palms facing each other. As you breathe in deeply through your nose, open your arms out to the sides as far as possible, bringing them slightly backward so you feel your chest opening. Hold the air for 2 seconds, then breathe out as you bring your hands forward again.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain relaxed cervical and shoulder posture. Use a slow, unforced respiratory cycle and allow a complete, gradual exhalation.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force inhalation or exhalation, hyperventilate, or hold the breath. Stop if dizziness or unusual breathlessness occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Thoracic Expansion

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the thoracic cage and pectoral region during horizontal adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand facing a flat wall, about one step away. Place the palms of your hands on the wall at chest height, keeping your arms straight. Slowly bend your elbows out to the sides to bring your face and chest closer to the wall, while keeping your body straight. Then push through your hands to return to the starting position with your arms straight.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the thoracic cage and pectoral region during horizontal adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both arms extended laterally at shoulder height. Move the arms forward into horizontal adduction until the wrists cross in front of the sternum. Return slowly to the starting position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This breathing exercise is intended to improve controlled respiratory mechanics of the thoracic cage and pectoral region, with emphasis on lateral costal expansion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright and place both hands over the lateral lower ribs. Inhale slowly through the nose, directing expansion into the hands. Exhale gradually and allow the rib cage to return to its resting position. Repeat for 5 respiratory cycles.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain relaxed cervical and shoulder posture. Use a slow, unforced respiratory cycle and allow a complete, gradual exhalation.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force inhalation or exhalation, hyperventilate, or hold the breath. Stop if dizziness or unusual breathlessness occurs.

esercizi.nome: Seated Isometric Pectoral Press with Cushion
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the thoracic cage and pectoral region, with emphasis on horizontal adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair. Hold a soft cushion in front of your chest between your forearms, keeping your elbows bent. Gently press your forearms inward to squeeze the cushion. Hold the pressure for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Isometric Pectoral Press with Cushion

esercizi.description: This breathing exercise is intended to improve controlled respiratory mechanics of the thoracic cage and pectoral region, with emphasis on thoracic rib expansion.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine and wrap the arms across the chest in a comfortable self-hug. Inhale slowly and deeply, directing the breath into the upper chest and sides of the rib cage so the ribs gently expand against the arms. Exhale and relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain relaxed cervical and shoulder posture. Use a slow, unforced respiratory cycle and allow a complete, gradual exhalation.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force inhalation or exhalation, hyperventilate, or hold the breath. Stop if dizziness or unusual breathlessness occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region during controlled stabilization.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright away from the backrest with both feet supported. Exhale slowly while drawing the lower abdominal wall inward without moving the spine or pelvis. Maintain the contraction for 4 seconds while continuing to breathe, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Seated Alternating Hip Flexion with Trunk Stabilization
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region during controlled stabilization.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright near the front of a chair with both feet supported. Activate the abdominal wall, then lift one knee a few centimetres without changing trunk or pelvic alignment. Lower slowly and alternate sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Alternating Hip Flexion with Trunk Stabilization

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region during lateral flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a stable chair with the feet positioned apart. Slide one hand toward the floor while laterally flexing the trunk. Return to neutral using controlled abdominal activation, then repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Seated Isometric Abdominal Bracing with Manual Resistance
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region, with emphasis on static stabilization.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both feet supported and place the palms over the distal thighs. During a slow exhalation, apply downward pressure through the hands while activating the abdominal wall without changing trunk position. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Isometric Abdominal Bracing with Manual Resistance

esercizi.nome: Seated Isometric Heel Press for Trunk Stabilization
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region, with emphasis on static stabilization.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on the front half of a chair with your feet resting on the floor. Place your hands on your thighs. Gently press both heels downward into the floor while slightly tightening your abdominal muscles. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Isometric Heel Press for Trunk Stabilization

esercizi.description: This contralateral isometric exercise challenges abdominal and lumbopelvic control by requiring the trunk to resist rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both feet supported. Elevate the right knee slightly and place the left palm on the distal anterior thigh. Press the thigh upward and the hand downward with equal submaximal force while preventing movement of the trunk and pelvis. Hold for 5 seconds, then repeat with the opposite hand and knee.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain a neutral spine, keep both shoulders level, and resist any tendency for the trunk or pelvis to rotate while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not lean backward, rotate the trunk, elevate the shoulder, hold the breath, or use maximal force.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region during controlled stabilization.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine on a mat with your knees bent and your feet resting on the floor. Tighten your abdominal muscles slightly. Lift your right foot a few centimetres from the floor and gently tap the heel forward, then bring it back to the starting position. Repeat 5 times, then switch legs.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region during lateral flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Set up in a side plank from the knees or feet. Lift the hips away from the floor, lower with control, and repeat.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region, with emphasis on static stabilization.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie on the back and press the lower back gently toward the floor. Lift the legs and arms only as far as you can keep control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This breathing exercise is intended to improve controlled respiratory mechanics of the abdominal wall and lumbopelvic region, with emphasis on diaphragmatic breathing and abdominal expansion.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the knees flexed. Place one hand over the upper chest and the other over the abdomen. Inhale slowly through the nose, allowing the abdominal wall to rise while limiting upper-chest movement. Exhale gradually and allow the abdomen to return.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain relaxed cervical and shoulder posture. Use a slow, unforced respiratory cycle and allow a complete, gradual exhalation.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force inhalation or exhalation, hyperventilate, or hold the breath. Stop if dizziness or unusual breathlessness occurs.

esercizi.nome: Seated Ball Transfer Around the Trunk
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair and hold a small soft ball or cushion with both hands. Pass the object from one hand to the other around your waist, moving it behind your back and then back to the front. Make 5 slow circles in one direction, then 5 in the opposite direction.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Ball Transfer Around the Trunk

esercizi.nome: Quadruped Contralateral Arm and Leg Extension
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the spine during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Assume a quadruped position on a padded surface. Slowly extend your right arm forward and your left leg backward at the same time. Hold the position for 2 seconds, then return to the starting position. Repeat with the left arm and right leg. Alternate slowly for 5 repetitions on each side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Quadruped Contralateral Arm and Leg Extension

esercizi.nome: Seated Anterior and Posterior Pelvic Tilt
esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled anterior pelvic tilt and posterior pelvic tilt of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit near the front of a chair with both feet supported and the hands resting on the thighs. Move the pelvis into anterior tilt with a small increase in lumbar extension, then into posterior tilt with gentle lumbar flexion. Alternate slowly for 10 repetitions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Anterior and Posterior Pelvic Tilt

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the knees flexed, the feet fully supported, and the arms alongside the trunk. Activate the gluteal muscles and extend the hips to elevate the pelvis a short distance. Hold for 3 seconds, then lower the spine and pelvis gradually.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region, with emphasis on abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both feet supported. Place an elastic band around the distal thighs or place both hands against the lateral aspects of the knees. Abduct the hips against the external resistance without changing foot position. Hold for 5 seconds, then return slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise challenges postural control and lower-limb stability during controlled lateral weight shift of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair with your feet resting on the floor. Without lifting your gluteal region, slowly shift your weight toward the right side of your pelvis, then return to the centre. Repeat toward the left side. Alternate slowly for 10 repetitions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Use a stable support when required. Maintain neutral lower-limb alignment and perform each movement slowly under control.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not continue without stable support if balance is uncertain. Avoid rapid weight shifts or loss of lower-limb alignment.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet grounded. Press through the feet and lift the hips into a bridge, then hold while breathing.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled anterior pelvic tilt and posterior pelvic tilt of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the knees bent and the feet flat. Gently tilt the pelvis backward to reduce the space under the lower back, then tilt it forward to restore a small natural arch. Continue rocking slowly between the two positions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise challenges postural control and lower-limb stability during controlled anterior pelvic tilt and posterior pelvic tilt of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the feet about hip-width apart and the knees softly bent. Tilt the pelvis backward by gently tucking the tailbone, then tilt it forward to return to a small natural lower-back curve. Alternate slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Use a stable support when required. Maintain neutral lower-limb alignment and perform each movement slowly under control.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not continue without stable support if balance is uncertain. Avoid rapid weight shifts or loss of lower-limb alignment.

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled anterior pelvic translation and posterior pelvic translation of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and the hands on the hips. Keeping the chest steady, glide the pelvis forward, return to centre, then glide it backward and return again.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise challenges postural control and lower-limb stability during controlled lateral weight shift of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and the hands on the hips. Glide the pelvis to the right, return to centre, then glide it to the left while keeping both feet in contact with the floor.
esercizi.whatToDo: Use a stable support when required. Maintain neutral lower-limb alignment and perform each movement slowly under control.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not continue without stable support if balance is uncertain. Avoid rapid weight shifts or loss of lower-limb alignment.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region during anterior pelvic translation, lateral weight shift, and posterior pelvic translation.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and the hands on the hips. Move the pelvis forward, then right, then backward, then left to draw a square. Return to centre and repeat in the opposite direction.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Standing Pelvic Circumduction with Trunk Stabilization
esercizi.description: This exercise challenges postural control and lower-limb stability during controlled circumduction of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with the feet slightly apart and the hands on the hips. Glide the pelvis forward, to one side, backward, and to the other side to complete a slow circle. Repeat in both directions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Use a stable support when required. Maintain neutral lower-limb alignment and perform each movement slowly under control.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not continue without stable support if balance is uncertain. Avoid rapid weight shifts or loss of lower-limb alignment.
esercizi.imageAlt: Standing Pelvic Circumduction with Trunk Stabilization

esercizi.nome: Seated Bilateral Shoulder Extension with Scapular Retraction
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during scapular retraction and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright away from the backrest with both arms elevated forward. Flex the elbows and draw them downward beside the trunk while retracting the scapulae. Hold for 3 seconds, then extend the arms upward again.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Bilateral Shoulder Extension with Scapular Retraction

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both feet supported and the arms crossed over the chest. Maintain the pelvis in neutral and rotate the thorax and head to one side through the available comfortable range. Hold for 3 seconds, return to neutral, and repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during rotation and lateral flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both feet supported and the hands resting on the thighs. Reach one arm diagonally upward across the midline with controlled trunk rotation. Return to neutral and repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Standing Axial Spine Elongation at Wall
esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with your back against a wall. Keep your feet slightly away from the wall and your knees softly bent. Gently press the middle and upper part of your back against the wall while lengthening the top of your head toward the ceiling. Hold this position for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Standing Axial Spine Elongation at Wall

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit on the front half of a chair with your hands resting on your thighs. Gently slide your hands slightly backward along your thighs while lifting your chest and lengthening your spine. Hold the tall position for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the spine during flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both feet supported and the arms extended forward at chest height. Flex the trunk slightly to reach forward, then activate the spinal extensor and abdominal muscles to return to the upright position. Repeat slowly for 5 repetitions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Segmental Quadruped Spinal Flexion and Extension
esercizi.description: This motor-control exercise develops sequential flexion and extension through the pelvis, lumbar spine, thoracic spine, and cervical spine.
esercizi.howToDo: Assume a quadruped position with the hands beneath the shoulders and the knees beneath the hips. Initiate a posterior pelvic tilt and progressively flex the lumbar, thoracic, and cervical regions. Reverse the sequence from the pelvis to return through neutral into comfortable extension. Complete 5 slow cycles.
esercizi.whatToDo: Move one spinal region after another, distribute the motion gradually, and coordinate flexion with exhalation and extension with inhalation.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not move the entire spine as one rigid block, collapse between the shoulders, force end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Segmental Quadruped Spinal Flexion and Extension

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright with your feet slightly apart. Hold a stick horizontally in front of your chest with both hands, keeping your elbows bent. Slowly rotate your torso to the right, keeping your pelvis facing forward. Return to the centre, then rotate to the left. Repeat 5 times on each side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Standing Segmental Spinal Flexion and Extension
esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled flexion and extension of the spine.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall. Slowly roll the head, shoulders, and spine downward one segment at a time, then return to standing with the same control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Standing Segmental Spinal Flexion and Extension

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: From a comfortable position, reach the crown of the head away from the pelvis and gently lengthen through the spine, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Alternating Diagonal Trunk Flexion and Rotation
esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled flexion and rotation of the spine.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the feet comfortable. Reach one hand diagonally toward the opposite foot or toward the floor, then return and alternate sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Alternating Diagonal Trunk Flexion and Rotation

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled circumduction of the pelvis and lumbopelvic region.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the hands on the hips. Make slow circles with the pelvis in one direction, then repeat in the other direction.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This selective mobility exercise emphasizes flexion and extension of the thoracic spine while the lumbopelvic region remains relatively stable.
esercizi.howToDo: Assume a quadruped position and establish a neutral pelvis. Without deliberately tilting the pelvis, press the floor away to round the upper back, then allow the sternum to descend gently between the shoulders to extend the thoracic region. Repeat slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the abdominal wall gently active, concentrate the motion between the shoulder blades, and maintain even pressure through both hands and knees.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not substitute with large pelvic tilts, collapse the lumbar spine, bend the elbows, or force thoracic end range.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit tall with the feet grounded. Rotate the trunk to one side, pause, return to centre, then repeat to the other side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Supported Trunk Flexion Latissimus Dorsi Stretch
esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on lateral flexion and flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Hold a stable support with the hands. Sit the hips back and let the side of the trunk lengthen until the lat area stretches.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Supported Trunk Flexion Latissimus Dorsi Stretch

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the spine, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit with the legs extended forward. Hinge forward from the hips and let the spine fold only through the available comfortable range.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on lateral flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit or stand tall. Reach one arm overhead and bend gently to the opposite side until the side of the trunk lengthens.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on rotation and flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Assume a quadruped position. Slide one arm under the opposite arm and rotate the upper back until the shoulder approaches the floor.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Sustained Prone Press-Up for Spinal Extension
esercizi.description: This sustained exercise exposes the spine to a comfortable extension position maintained for a short static hold.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie prone with the hands under or slightly ahead of the shoulders. Press through the hands to elevate the chest while keeping the pelvis supported. Stop at the available comfortable extension range, hold for 5 to 10 seconds while breathing normally, then lower completely.
esercizi.whatToDo: Distribute the extension through the spine, keep the shoulders away from the ears, and maintain a symptom-free static position.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not lift the pelvis, force the elbows straight, hold the breath, or continue if pain radiates or progressively increases.
esercizi.imageAlt: Sustained Prone Press-Up for Spinal Extension

esercizi.nome: Wall-Assisted Thoracic Extension with Arm Slide
esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled extension and scapular retraction of the spine.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the back close to a wall. Slide the arms upward and downward while keeping the ribs controlled and the upper back active.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Wall-Assisted Thoracic Extension with Arm Slide

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand facing a wall with the hands resting on it. Let the chest move gently forward and upward while keeping the hips controlled.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit tall and rotate the trunk to one side. Use the hands lightly for support and hold the twist while breathing.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Dynamic Prone Press-Up for Spinal Extension
esercizi.description: This dynamic mobility exercise uses repeated press-up cycles to move the spine into and out of a comfortable extension range.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie prone with the hands near the shoulders. Press through the hands to lift the chest through the available comfortable extension range, then lower fully to the starting position without holding at the top. Repeat at a slow, even tempo.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the pelvis supported, relax fully between repetitions, and make each upward and downward phase smooth and controlled.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not pause in a sustained hold, use momentum, force the elbows straight, or continue if pain radiates or progressively increases.
esercizi.imageAlt: Dynamic Prone Press-Up for Spinal Extension

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on lateral flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Set up in a comfortable lunge. Reach one arm overhead and bend gently away from the back leg, then return.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled rotation of the spine.
esercizi.howToDo: Assume a quadruped position. Slide one arm under the opposite arm to rotate, then open the same arm toward the ceiling.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the spine, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Assume a quadruped position. Press through the hands and move the spine into flexion while allowing the head to follow the spinal curve. Maintain the position while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the spine, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Assume a quadruped position. Let the chest move forward and the sit bones lift slightly, creating a gentle arch.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Seated Segmental Spinal Flexion and Extension
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit tall with the legs extended or knees bent. Slowly roll the spine backward or forward within a comfortable range, then return.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Segmental Spinal Flexion and Extension

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled extension of the spine.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the back facing a wall. Reach the hands overhead to the wall, then slowly walk them down only as far as control allows.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Supported Forward Fold with Alternating Knee Extension
esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the spine, with emphasis on flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Fold forward with the hands supported. Alternate gently bending and straightening the knees while keeping the spine movement controlled.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Supported Forward Fold with Alternating Knee Extension

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled extension of the spine.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall and extend both arms overhead. Keeping the pelvis controlled, lift the chest and move the hands slightly backward to create a gentle extension through the upper and middle spine, then return to neutral.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Standing Trunk Flexion with Chest-Led Descent
esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled flexion of the spine.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the knees softly bent. Begin the descent by guiding the chest forward and down, then allow the head and arms to follow toward the floor. Stop at a comfortable depth and return slowly to standing.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Standing Trunk Flexion with Chest-Led Descent

esercizi.nome: Seated Isometric Thoracic Extension Against Backrest
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the spine, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit with the thoracic spine supported against the chair backrest. Press the upper back gently into the support while elongating the spine vertically. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Isometric Thoracic Extension Against Backrest

esercizi.nome: Seated Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Thoracic Extension
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during extension and scapular retraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit away from the backrest or stand. Keep your arms by your sides. Close your hands into fists, keeping your thumbs pointing upward. Slowly lift your arms out to the sides up to shoulder height and bring them slightly backward, always keeping your thumbs pointing toward the ceiling. Hold for 3 seconds while feeling your back muscles working, then slowly lower your arms back down.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Thoracic Extension

esercizi.nome: Dynamic Prone Upper-Trunk Extension with Forehead Support
esercizi.description: This dynamic exercise develops short-range thoracic extensor control with the head and upper limbs supported as one unit.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie prone with the hands stacked beneath the forehead. Keep the forehead in light contact with the hands and lift the hands, head, and upper chest together a few centimetres from the floor. Lower immediately with control and repeat for 5 repetitions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the cervical spine neutral, emphasize movement through the upper trunk, and complete each repetition without a prolonged hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not lift the chin, separate the forehead from the hands, use momentum, or exaggerate lumbar extension.
esercizi.imageAlt: Dynamic Prone Upper-Trunk Extension with Forehead Support

esercizi.nome: Prone Isometric Trunk Extension with Arms Alongside Body
esercizi.description: This isometric exercise develops endurance of the spinal extensor chain with the arms positioned alongside the trunk.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie prone with both arms alongside the body and the palms facing inward. Gently lift the head and chest a small distance while keeping the cervical spine neutral. Hold the position for 5 seconds, lower completely, and rest before repeating.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain abdominal control, lengthen through the crown of the head, and use a low sustained lift while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not swing the arms, lift the chin, hold the breath, force lumbar extension, or raise the trunk as high as possible.
esercizi.imageAlt: Prone Isometric Trunk Extension with Arms Alongside Body

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the spine during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie prone with the legs long and the arms extended in front. Gently brace the abdomen, then lift the chest, arms, and legs a small distance from the floor. Pause briefly and lower with control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the spine during extension, scapular retraction, and horizontal abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie prone with the arms extended to the sides at shoulder height. Keep the thumbs pointing upward or the palms facing down, gently lift the chest and arms a small distance, then make short controlled up-and-down wing pulses before lowering.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force spinal end range, or continue if sharp or radiating pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Seated Pelvic Floor and Gluteal Contraction
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve voluntary activation, relaxation, and motor control of the pelvic floor, with emphasis on controlled contraction and complete relaxation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both feet supported. Contract the pelvic floor and gluteal muscles simultaneously, drawing the pelvic floor gently upward. Hold for 5 seconds while breathing normally, then relax completely.
esercizi.whatToDo: Coordinate the contraction with normal breathing and allow complete muscular relaxation between repetitions.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, contract maximally, or maintain residual tension between repetitions.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Pelvic Floor and Gluteal Contraction

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve voluntary activation, relaxation, and motor control of the pelvic floor, with emphasis on controlled contraction and complete relaxation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a firm chair with both feet supported. Contract and elevate the pelvic floor muscles without activating the abdominal wall excessively. Hold for 4 seconds while breathing normally, then release gradually.
esercizi.whatToDo: Coordinate the contraction with normal breathing and allow complete muscular relaxation between repetitions.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, contract maximally, or maintain residual tension between repetitions.

esercizi.nome: Seated Hip Adduction with Pelvic Floor Contraction
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve voluntary activation, relaxation, and motor control of the pelvic floor, with emphasis on adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both feet supported and place a soft ball or folded cushion between the knees. During a slow exhalation, adduct the hips to compress the object while performing a gentle pelvic floor contraction. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax completely.
esercizi.whatToDo: Coordinate the contraction with normal breathing and allow complete muscular relaxation between repetitions.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, contract maximally, or maintain residual tension between repetitions.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Hip Adduction with Pelvic Floor Contraction

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve voluntary activation, relaxation, and motor control of the pelvic floor, with emphasis on controlled contraction and complete relaxation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit near the front of a stable chair with both feet supported. Before initiating the transfer, perform a gentle pelvic floor contraction. Maintain the contraction while inclining the trunk forward and extending the hips and knees to stand. Relax fully once upright.
esercizi.whatToDo: Coordinate the contraction with normal breathing and allow complete muscular relaxation between repetitions.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, contract maximally, or maintain residual tension between repetitions.

esercizi.nome: Supine Hip Abduction and Adduction with Pelvic Floor Control
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve voluntary activation, relaxation, and motor control of the pelvic floor, with emphasis on abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the knees flexed and the feet together. Allow both knees to move laterally into hip abduction, then return them to neutral while coordinating a gentle pelvic floor contraction.
esercizi.whatToDo: Coordinate the contraction with normal breathing and allow complete muscular relaxation between repetitions.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, contract maximally, or maintain residual tension between repetitions.
esercizi.imageAlt: Supine Hip Abduction and Adduction with Pelvic Floor Control

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve voluntary activation, relaxation, and motor control of the pelvic floor, with emphasis on controlled contraction and complete relaxation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a firm chair with both feet supported. Perform a brief pelvic floor contraction followed by complete relaxation. Repeat 5 times with a short rest between contractions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Coordinate the contraction with normal breathing and allow complete muscular relaxation between repetitions.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, contract maximally, or maintain residual tension between repetitions.
